scope: Memoized MPU region lookups in the vendored CPU. Guest-visible behavior is unchanged; this records the throughput recovered and how the cache was proved not to go stale.
change: Ppb owns a permission cache: six front lanes, one per (access kind, privileged) pair, ahead of a 128-entry direct-mapped table of 32-byte blocks. Region permissions are constant across a 32-byte block, so a block never spans a permission boundary. Every MPU register write calls Ppb::mpu_changed(), which discards the cache, so a lookup carries no validity check at all.
method: crates/qemu-emery/examples/native_boot.rs, release build, unchanged official 4.37.0 images, fixed epoch, 8 virtual seconds, median of 3 runs on one host core. All four builds measured on the same machine in the same session.
summary: MPU enforcement cost 42% (Flint), 27% (Emery) and 28% (Gabbro) of pre-enforcement boot throughput; it now costs 16%, 18% and 19%. Flint gains most because PMSAv7 decodes a region size per lookup where PMSAv8 compares a stored limit.
checksRemovedNote: A build of this tree with the MPU check stubbed out reaches 20.3 to 20.9 M steps/s, not the 22.1 M of the pre-enforcement commit. About a third of the remaining gap is the precise-fault machinery added with MPU precision, not region lookup, so it is not recoverable by caching.

lookupProfile.method: Temporary counters over an 8 virtual second boot, removed before commit
lookupProfile.note: About 1.66 lookups per executed instruction, and 98.9% of them never reach a region scan. The remaining cost is the volume of lookups, not the scan.

equivalence.firmwareBoots: All three 20 virtual second 4.37.0 boots are byte-identical to 9864a93: same steps, cycles, frames and frame, RAM and UART digests
equivalence.startupCheckpoints: npm run build:checkpoints reproduces identical SHA-256 checkpoints across repeated runs
equivalence.staleness: Debug builds re-scan the regions behind every cache hit and assert the answers match. The 162 Rust workspace tests pass under that assertion, and a debug boot of unchanged 4.37.0 firmware ran 38.7 M (Flint), 40.9 M (Emery) and 41.2 M (Gabbro) instructions, roughly 65 M re-scanned lookups per profile, with no mismatch.

validation.browserGates: Preview and demo gates pass in Chromium: 9020 ms first boot and install, 10.271 virtual seconds in 10 real seconds, and native-QEMU notification frames match on all three profiles
validation.notRun: Firefox and WebKit engines, the sensor workflow gate and the compatibility census, as for the MPU precision change

limits: Host throughput on one x86-64 machine, not browser or watch performance
The cache is derived state and is never checkpointed; a restored core refills it
A writer that sets MPU registers without going through the register path must call Ppb::mpu_changed(); the debug assertion is what enforces this in tests
